raw_response:
Hm, let me think about this year's planting...

I've been farming these 12 mu for a long time now, same as my mother-in-law did before me. Wheat and maize, wheat and maize — that's what grows here, that's what everyone does. My husband works construction in town most of the year, so it's mostly me and the kids in the fields, though my oldest is in school now so I can't count on him except on weekends and during busy times.

The wheat's already in the ground — I planted it back in October like always, right after we pulled the maize out. Now I'm thinking about the topdressing in spring and getting ready for maize after the wheat comes off in June.

For the wheat, I did what I always do at planting. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before ploughing — that's the 复合肥, the one with three numbers on it, the seed shop sells it. Twelve bags for my twelve mu. I bought decent seed from the co-op, same variety as last year because it did alright — maybe 400 kg per mu, nothing special but no disaster either. Now when the wheat starts to green up after winter, around Qingming time, I'll spread about half a bag of 尿素 per mu. If the wheat looks yellow or thin in some spots, I'll put a bit more there. My neighbor 李嫂 always says "don't be stingy with the spring fertilizer" and she's usually right — the wheat tells you if it's hungry.

I'll water the wheat probably three times — once now when it greens up, once at jointing, and once when it's filling the grain. The well works fine but the electricity isn't cheap, and I have to take turns with the others on our side of the village. If it rains good in April-May I'll skip one watering to save money. For weeds I'll spray once in spring, the shop owner tells me what to buy, I just do what he says since it's worked before.

Then comes the hard part — after wheat harvest in early June, we've got maybe a week to get the maize in. I hire the combine to cut the wheat, then right away I hire someone with the no-till seeder to plant the maize into the stubble. Everyone does this now, no time to plough. I plant the hybrid maize seed the co-op recommends, last year it did about 450 kg/mu so I'll use the same one. With the maize I put the fertilizer down when I plant — one bag of compound per mu, and then when the maize is about knee-high I'll topdress some urea, maybe a third of a bag per mu. Maize doesn't need as much fussing as wheat.

For maize I usually only irrigate once or twice — summer rains take care of most of it, and if it's a wet year I don't irrigate at all. I'll spray herbicide once after planting so the weeds don't choke the seedlings. If I see the corn borer showing up I'll spray once, otherwise no.

Money's always tight. My husband sends some home, and what we made from maize last fall is mostly gone to winter expenses and the wheat planting fertilizer. I'll have to buy the spring urea soon, and the maize inputs come due in June. If the price of fertilizer goes up too much I'll cut back a little, maybe not the full half-bag of urea on the wheat. But I won't cut the seed or the base fertilizer — that's asking for a bad harvest.
